Problem

For a series RLC circuit, R = 40 Ω, L = 4 H, C = 1/4 F. Calculate the characteristic roots and classify the response.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 2 steps

  1. Find the two parameters

    Use the series RLC damping factor.

    α=R2L=5 s−1,ω0=1LC=1 rad/s\alpha=\frac{R}{2L}=5\ \mathrm{s^{-1}},\quad\omega_0=\frac1{\sqrt{LC}}=1\ \mathrm{rad/s}α=2LR​=5 s−1,ω0​=LC​1​=1 rad/s

  2. Compare, then calculate the roots

    Alpha is greater than omega-zero: two different real roots.

    s1,2=−5±25−1=−5±24s_{1,2}=-5\pm\sqrt{25-1}=-5\pm\sqrt{24}s1,2​=−5±25−1​=−5±24​
Result
s1=−0.10102,s2=−9.89898 s−1(overdamped)s_1=-0.10102,\quad s_2=-9.89898\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\quad(\text{overdamped})s1​=−0.10102,s2​=−9.89898 s−1(overdamped)

Check. The roots sum to −10 and multiply to 1, matching s² + 10s + 1 = 0.

Problem

The circuit is at steady state before the switch opens. Find the indicated inductor current i(t) for t > 0.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 4 steps

  1. Find the initial stored values

    Before switching, the capacitor branch is open and the inductor is short.

    i0=104+6=1 A,vC0=6 Vi_0=\frac{10}{4+6}=1\ \mathrm A,\quad v_{C0}=6\ \mathrm Vi0​=4+610​=1 A,vC0​=6 V

  2. Reduce the loop after switching

    The source is removed. The 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors are now in the discharge loop.

    R=9 Ω,α=92(0.5)=9,ω0=10.5(0.02)=10,ωd=19R=9\ \Omega,\quad\alpha=\frac9{2(0.5)}=9,\quad\omega_0=\frac1{\sqrt{0.5(0.02)}}=10,\quad\omega_d=\sqrt{19}R=9 Ω,α=2(0.5)9​=9,ω0​=0.5(0.02)​1​=10,ωd​=19​

  3. Find the starting slope

    The capacitor voltage drives the chosen current. KVL gives L i′ + 9i − vC = 0.

    i0′=6−9(1)0.5=−6 A/si'_0=\frac{6-9(1)}{0.5}=-6\ \mathrm{A/s}i0′​=0.56−9(1)​=−6 A/s

  4. Fit the underdamped form

    The initial value fixes A; the initial slope fixes B.

    i=e−9t(Acos⁡19t+Bsin⁡19t),A=1,−9A+19B=−6i=e^{-9t}(A\cos\sqrt{19}t+B\sin\sqrt{19}t),\quad A=1,\quad-9A+\sqrt{19}B=-6i=e−9t(Acos19​t+Bsin19​t),A=1,−9A+19​B=−6
Result
i(t)=e−9t[cos⁡(19t)+319sin⁡(19t)] Ai(t)=e^{-9t}\left[\cos(\sqrt{19}t)+\frac3{\sqrt{19}}\sin(\sqrt{19}t)\right]\ \mathrm Ai(t)=e−9t[cos(19​t)+19​3​sin(19​t)] A

Check. At t = 0, i = 1 A and i′ = −6 A/s. With the source removed the response decays to zero.

Lecture exampleExample 8.5 · Three damping casesReviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Find v(t) in the parallel RLC circuit with v(0) = 5 V, iL(0) = 0, L = 1 H and C = 10 mF. Consider R = 1.923 Ω, 5 Ω and 6.25 Ω.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 4 steps

  1. Use one setup for all three cases

    All branch currents point down. Apply KCL at the top node.

    ω0=10,α=50R,v0′=−v0/R+iL0C=−500R\omega_0=10,\quad\alpha=\frac{50}{R},\quad v'_0=-\frac{v_0/R+i_{L0}}C=-\frac{500}{R}ω0​=10,α=R50​,v0′​=−Cv0​/R+iL0​​=−R500​

  2. R = 1.923 Ω: overdamped

    Using the intended rounded alpha = 26, the roots are approximately −2 and −50. Solve for two constants.

    A+B=5,−2A−50B=−260 ⇒ A=−524, B=12524A+B=5,\quad-2A-50B=-260\ \Rightarrow\ A=-\frac5{24},\ B=\frac{125}{24}A+B=5,−2A−50B=−260 ⇒ A=−245​, B=24125​

  3. R = 5 Ω: critically damped

    Alpha equals omega-zero. Use (A + Bt) exp(−10t).

    A=5,B−10A=−100 ⇒ B=−50A=5,\quad B-10A=-100\ \Rightarrow\ B=-50A=5,B−10A=−100 ⇒ B=−50

  4. R = 6.25 Ω: underdamped

    Alpha = 8 and damped frequency = 6.

    A=5,−8A+6B=−80 ⇒ B=−203A=5,\quad-8A+6B=-80\ \Rightarrow\ B=-\frac{20}3A=5,−8A+6B=−80 ⇒ B=−320​
Result
R=1.923: v≈−0.2083e−2t+5.2083e−50tR=5: v=(5−50t)e−10tR=6.25: v=e−8t(5cos⁡6t−6.6667sin⁡6t)V\begin{aligned}R=1.923:&\ v\approx-0.2083e^{-2t}+5.2083e^{-50t}\\R=5:&\ v=(5-50t)e^{-10t}\\R=6.25:&\ v=e^{-8t}(5\cos6t-6.6667\sin6t)\end{aligned}\quad\mathrm VR=1.923:R=5:R=6.25:​ v≈−0.2083e−2t+5.2083e−50t v=(5−50t)e−10t v=e−8t(5cos6t−6.6667sin6t)​V

Check. Each result begins at 5 V and decays to zero. The first case uses rounded roots because 1.923 Ω is rounded.

Worked solution · 4 steps

  1. Find the pre-switch state

    The left inductor carries the isolated 4 A source current. On the right, the capacitor voltage is set by two 20 Ω resistors.

    i0=4 A,v0=302020+20=15 Vi_0=4\ \mathrm A,\quad v_0=30\frac{20}{20+20}=15\ \mathrm Vi0​=4 A,v0​=3020+2020​=15 V

  2. Find the circuit after zero

    The voltage source becomes a short. The two 20 Ω resistors are parallel, and the inductor eventually carries all 4 A.

    R=10, L=20, C=0.008, i∞=4, i0′=1520=0.75R=10,\ L=20,\ C=0.008,\ i_\infty=4,\ i'_0=\frac{15}{20}=0.75R=10, L=20, C=0.008, i∞​=4, i0′​=2015​=0.75

  3. Calculate the roots and constants

    The response is overdamped. Use i = 4 + A exp(s1 t) + B exp(s2 t).

    α=6.25, ω0=2.5, s1,2=−6.25±32.8125;A+B=0, (s1−s2)A=0.75\alpha=6.25,\ \omega_0=2.5,\ s_{1,2}=-6.25\pm\sqrt{32.8125};\quad A+B=0,\ (s_1-s_2)A=0.75α=6.25, ω0​=2.5, s1,2​=−6.25±32.8125​;A+B=0, (s1​−s2​)A=0.75

  4. Recover the resistor current

    The indicated resistor is 20 Ω, even though the equivalent resistance is 10 Ω.

    v=Ldidt,iR=v20=2020didtv=L\frac{di}{dt},\quad i_R=\frac v{20}=\frac{20}{20}\frac{di}{dt}v=Ldtdi​,iR​=20v​=2020​dtdi​
Result
i(t)=4+0.065465(e−0.52178t−e−11.97822t) AiR(t)=0.065465(−0.52178e−0.52178t+11.97822e−11.97822t) A\begin{aligned}i(t)&=4+0.065465(e^{-0.52178t}-e^{-11.97822t})\ \mathrm A\\i_R(t)&=0.065465(-0.52178e^{-0.52178t}+11.97822e^{-11.97822t})\ \mathrm A\end{aligned}i(t)iR​(t)​=4+0.065465(e−0.52178t−e−11.97822t) A=0.065465(−0.52178e−0.52178t+11.97822e−11.97822t) A​

Check. At zero iR = 0.75 A and v = 15 V. At infinity i = 4 A and iR = 0.

    Req2(4)=5 ⇒ Req=40 Ω\frac{R_{eq}}{2(4)}=5\ \Rightarrow\ R_{eq}=40\ \Omega2(4)Req​​=5 ⇒ Req​=40 Ω

Problem setProblem Set 7 · Q3 · Problem 8.23Reviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Choose C so the parallel network is underdamped with alpha = 1 s⁻¹.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 3 steps

  1. Combine the capacitors

    The unknown C and the 10 mF capacitor share the same two nodes.

    CT=C+0.01 FC_T=C+0.01\ \mathrm FCT​=C+0.01 F

  2. Use the required damping factor

    For parallel RLC, alpha = 1/(2 R CT).

    1=12(10)CT ⇒ CT=0.05 F1=\frac1{2(10)C_T}\ \Rightarrow\ C_T=0.05\ \mathrm F1=2(10)CT​1​ ⇒ CT​=0.05 F

  3. Subtract the existing capacitor and verify damping

    Use L = 20 mH = 0.020 H.

    C=0.05−0.01=0.04 F,ω0=10.020(0.05)=31.62>1C=0.05-0.01=0.04\ \mathrm F,\quad\omega_0=\frac1{\sqrt{0.020(0.05)}}=31.62>1C=0.05−0.01=0.04 F,ω0​=0.020(0.05)​1​=31.62>1
Result
C=40 mF(underdamped)C=40\ \mathrm{mF}\quad(\text{underdamped})C=40 mF(underdamped)

Check. The key prints omega-zero as 141.42; the pictured values give 31.62 rad/s. This arithmetic error does not change C or the damping classification.

Problem setProblem Set 7 · Q4 · Problem 8.47Reviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Find output voltage vo(t) after the switch closes in Fig. 8.94.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 4 steps

  1. Use the pre-switch DC circuit

    The capacitor is open and the inductor shorts its branch. Current divides between 5 Ω and 10 Ω.

    iL0=355+10=1 A,v0=0i_{L0}=3\frac5{5+10}=1\ \mathrm A,\quad v_0=0iL0​=35+105​=1 A,v0​=0

  2. Find the post-switch parameters

    The switch bypasses 10 Ω. R = 5 Ω, C = 0.01 F, L = 1 H.

    α=12(5)(0.01)=10=ω0=11(0.01)\alpha=\frac1{2(5)(0.01)}=10=\omega_0=\frac1{\sqrt{1(0.01)}}α=2(5)(0.01)1​=10=ω0​=1(0.01)​1​

  3. Solve for inductor current

    At infinity the inductor carries 3 A. Its starting slope is v0/L = 0.

    iL=3+(A+Bt)e−10t,A=−2,B−10A=0 ⇒ B=−20i_L=3+(A+Bt)e^{-10t},\quad A=-2,\quad B-10A=0\ \Rightarrow\ B=-20iL​=3+(A+Bt)e−10t,A=−2,B−10A=0 ⇒ B=−20

  4. Differentiate to get the requested voltage

    Use the passive voltage polarity across the inductor.

    vo=LdiLdt=ddt[3+(−2−20t)e−10t]v_o=L\frac{di_L}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left[3+(-2-20t)e^{-10t}\right]vo​=LdtdiL​​=dtd​[3+(−2−20t)e−10t]
Result
vo(t)=200te−10t V,t≥0v_o(t)=200t e^{-10t}\ \mathrm V,\quad t\ge0vo​(t)=200te−10t V,t≥0

Check. vo begins and ends at zero. KCL gives vo′(0) = (3−1)/0.01 = 200 V/s. In the key this is numbered 5, but it is assignment Q4.

Problem setProblem Set 7 · Q5 · Problem 8.49Reviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Find the indicated inductor current i(t) for t > 0 after the switch opens.

View source diagram / question page

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 3 steps

  1. Find initial and final currents

    Before switching, both sources feed the shorted inductor. After switching, only the 3 A source remains.

    i0=3+124=6 A,v0=0,i∞=3 Ai_0=3+\frac{12}{4}=6\ \mathrm A,\quad v_0=0,\quad i_\infty=3\ \mathrm Ai0​=3+412​=6 A,v0​=0,i∞​=3 A

  2. Classify the parallel RLC response

    Use R = 5 Ω, C = 1/20 F and L = 5 H.

    α=12(5)(0.05)=2,ω0=15(0.05)=2\alpha=\frac1{2(5)(0.05)}=2,\quad\omega_0=\frac1{\sqrt{5(0.05)}}=2α=2(5)(0.05)1​=2,ω0​=5(0.05)​1​=2

  3. Use the critically damped form

    The initial derivative is v0/L = 0.

    i=3+(A+Bt)e−2t,A=6−3=3,B−2A=0 ⇒ B=6i=3+(A+Bt)e^{-2t},\quad A=6-3=3,\quad B-2A=0\ \Rightarrow\ B=6i=3+(A+Bt)e−2t,A=6−3=3,B−2A=0 ⇒ B=6
Result
i(t)=3+(3+6t)e−2t A,t>0i(t)=3+(3+6t)e^{-2t}\ \mathrm A,\quad t>0i(t)=3+(3+6t)e−2t A,t>0

Check. i(0) = 6 A, i′(0) = 0, and i(∞) = 3 A. This is numbered 6 in the key but Q5 on the assignment.

Worked solution · 3 steps

  1. Transform the sources and find initial values

    Use the key’s pre-switch equivalent: a 30 V supply with 10 Ω and 5 Ω resistors. The marked pre-switch inductor current is opposite capacitor charging current.

    v0=30510+5=10 V,iC0=−2 A,v0′=−24=−0.5 V/sv_0=30\frac5{10+5}=10\ \mathrm V,\quad i_{C0}=-2\ \mathrm A,\quad v'_0=-\frac24=-0.5\ \mathrm{V/s}v0​=3010+55​=10 V,iC0​=−2 A,v0′​=−42​=−0.5 V/s

  2. Find the final value and poles

    After switching: Vs = 20 V, R = 5 Ω, L = 1 H and C = 4 F.

    v∞=20,α=2.5,ω0=0.5,s1,2=−2.5±6v_\infty=20,\quad\alpha=2.5,\quad\omega_0=0.5,\quad s_{1,2}=-2.5\pm\sqrt6v∞​=20,α=2.5,ω0​=0.5,s1,2​=−2.5±6​

  3. Fit both constants

    Use s1 = −4.94949 and s2 = −0.05051.

    v=20+Aes1t+Bes2t,A+B=−10,s1A+s2B=−0.5v=20+Ae^{s_1t}+Be^{s_2t},\quad A+B=-10,\quad s_1A+s_2B=-0.5v=20+Aes1​t+Bes2​t,A+B=−10,s1​A+s2​B=−0.5
Result
v(t)≈20+0.205166e−4.94949t−10.205166e−0.05051t Vv(t)\approx20+0.205166e^{-4.94949t}-10.205166e^{-0.05051t}\ \mathrm Vv(t)≈20+0.205166e−4.94949t−10.205166e−0.05051t V

Check. v(0) = 10 V, v′(0) = −0.5 V/s, and the final voltage is 20 V.

Question: ECET 250E-Linear Circuit 1-Quiz 1-Chapter1,2-2026 Solution2.pdf · page 1

Quiz reviewQuiz 1 · Question 2 · Differentiate chargeReviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Find the current if q(t) = (9e⁻³ᵗ − 2e⁻⁶ᵗ) nC.

View source diagram / question page (includes instructor answers)

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 2 steps

  1. Definition

    Current is the time derivative of charge.

    i=dqdti=\frac{dq}{dt}i=dtdq​

  2. Chain rule

    Multiply each exponential by the coefficient of t in its exponent.

    i(t)=9(−3)e−3t−2(−6)e−6ti(t)=9(-3)e^{-3t}-2(-6)e^{-6t}i(t)=9(−3)e−3t−2(−6)e−6t
Result
i(t)=(−27e−3t+12e−6t) nAi(t)=(-27e^{-3t}+12e^{-6t})\,\mathrm{nA}i(t)=(−27e−3t+12e−6t)nA

Check. At t = 0, i = −15 nA; the current tends to zero as t increases.

Problem

A current rises linearly from 0 A at 0 s to 2 A at 6 s. Find the charge transferred.

View source diagram / question page (includes instructor answers)

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 1 steps

  1. Area gives charge

    The current–time region is a triangle.

    Q=∫06i(t) dt=12(6)(2)Q=\int_0^6 i(t)\,dt=\frac12(6)(2)Q=∫06​i(t)dt=21​(6)(2)
Result
Q=6 CQ=6\,\mathrm CQ=6C

Check. A·s = C; average current 1 A for 6 s also gives 6 C.

Problem

Find charge from 0 to 8 s for the graph through (0,0), (2,8), (4,8), (5,3), (7,3), (8,0), with time in seconds and current in amperes.

View source diagram / question page (includes instructor answers)

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 2 steps

  1. Split at every corner

    Use triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids.

    Q0→2=8,Q2→4=16,Q4→5=8+32(1)=5.5Q_{0\to2}=8,\quad Q_{2\to4}=16,\quad Q_{4\to5}=\frac{8+3}{2}(1)=5.5Q0→2​=8,Q2→4​=16,Q4→5​=28+3​(1)=5.5

  2. Finish and sum

    All regions are above the time axis.

    Q5→7=6,Q7→8=1.5;Q=8+16+5.5+6+1.5Q_{5\to7}=6,\quad Q_{7\to8}=1.5;\quad Q=8+16+5.5+6+1.5Q5→7​=6,Q7→8​=1.5;Q=8+16+5.5+6+1.5
Result
Q=37 CQ=37\,\mathrm CQ=37C

Check. Every interval has positive current, so all areas add.

Result

Problem

A 21 A source supplies parallel branches: 3 Ω carrying iₒ downward, a dependent source 2iₒ downward, and 6 Ω with voltage vₒ positive at the top. Find vₒ.

View source diagram / question page (includes instructor answers)

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 2 steps

  1. Relate branch current to voltage

    All parallel branches share vₒ.

    io=vo3i_o=\frac{v_o}{3}io​=3vo​​

  2. Write KCL

    The upward 21 A source supplies all three downward currents.

    21=io+2io+vo6=7vo621=i_o+2i_o+\frac{v_o}{6}=\frac{7v_o}{6}21=io​+2io​+6vo​​=67vo​​
Result
vo=18 V,io=6 Av_o=18\,\mathrm V,\qquad i_o=6\,\mathrm Avo​=18V,io​=6A

Question: ECET 250E-Linear Circuit 1-Quiz 1-Chapter1,2-2026 Solution2.pdf · page 6

Quiz reviewQuiz 1 · Question 11 · Resistor-network reductionReviewed
Link to this problem

Problem

Find Rab for the network in the source diagram. Reduce it from the far-right branches toward terminals a and b.

View source diagram / question page (includes instructor answers)

Original page for topology, polarities, and reference directions. Some lecture and key pages also show answers. Open the original file for full resolution.

Worked solution · 4 steps

  1. Top parallel pair

    The 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors have the same two endpoints.

    10∥15=6 Ω10\parallel15=6\,\Omega10∥15=6Ω

  2. Right path

    Add the right 9 Ω resistor, then combine with the diagonal 10 Ω branch.

    (6+9)∥10=15∥10=6 Ω(6+9)\parallel10=15\parallel10=6\,\Omega(6+9)∥10=15∥10=6Ω

  3. Bottom path

    Add 3 Ω, then combine with the 18 Ω and 6 Ω branches.

    6+3=9;9∥18∥6=3 Ω6+3=9;\qquad 9\parallel18\parallel6=3\,\Omega6+3=9;9∥18∥6=3Ω

  4. Input resistor

    The remaining 9 Ω is in series with the reduced network.

    Rab=9+3R_{ab}=9+3Rab​=9+3
Result
Rab=12 ΩR_{ab}=12\,\OmegaRab​=12Ω

Check. The internal parallel combination is smaller than its smallest branch (6 Ω).
